summary.allegation: The issuer says the cardholder did not authorise the 1,240.50 EUR charge of 1 April 2025 and suggests the card details were compromised.
summary.to_defend: Mastercard requires any two of the listed compelling evidence items, such as a full AVS plus CVV match, successful Identity Check authentication, two prior undisputed transactions or signed delivery to the billing address.

requirements.title: AVS and CVV match
requirements.text: AVS match (full address) AND CVV match on the disputed transaction.
requirements.finding: Transaction metadata and the gateway authorisation log both record a full address AVS match (Y) and a CVV match (M) on txn_4412EF.

citations.quote:
AVS check (full address)
Y
Full match

requirements.title: 3DS authenticated
requirements.text: 3D Secure authentication completed successfully (Mastercard SecureCode / Identity Check).
requirements.finding: Mastercard Identity Check completed successfully for this transaction with ECI 02, an authentication value and a DS transaction ID, timestamped seconds before authorisation.

requirements.title: Two prior undisputed transactions
requirements.text: Two prior undisputed transactions from the same cardholder with this merchant in the past 12 months, with matching billing details.
requirements.finding: No transaction history was supplied; the only related datapoint is a device fingerprint noted as a returning device, which does not identify two prior undisputed transactions or matching billing details.
requirements.gap: No record of two prior undisputed purchases by this cardholder in the past 12 months with matching billing details.

requirements.title: Signed delivery to billing address
requirements.text: Proof of delivery to the cardholder's billing address with signature.
requirements.finding: MCC 7512 is vehicle rental and the booking involved no shipment of goods, so signed proof of delivery to the billing address cannot exist for this transaction.

reasons: Every requirement the decision relies on is backed by verified evidence

checks.label: Key evidence comes from document text, not only from an image
Images the evidence relies on are fully legible
Every quoted passage was found in the documents
The disputed charge matches the merchant's own records
The rule check and the AI recommendation agree

justification: Represent: R1 (full AVS plus CVV match) and R2 (successful Identity Check authentication) are both satisfied, meeting the any two requirement.
rationale:
The cardholder disputes a 1,240.50 EUR charge of 1 April 2025 as unauthorised.
Transaction txn_4412EF returned a full address AVS match (Y) and a CVV match (M) at authorisation, evidenced by the gateway authorisation log.
Mastercard Identity Check authenticated the cardholder with the issuing bank at 2025-04-01 11:08:18 UTC, ECI 02, authentication ID ic_77f31a82bb, DS transaction ID ds_4b2e1100c4.
The order was placed from a Paris IP address (90.84.21.117) on a device previously seen with this merchant, matching the FR-issued card and the 75011 billing postcode.
Two of the required compelling evidence items are met, so the chargeback is defended and the amount should be represented.
analyst_notes: If available, ask the merchant for two prior undisputed orders on this card in the last 12 months to add R3 as a third item.
D2 asserts that liability rests with the issuer; keep the filing to the factual authentication data rather than repeating that claim.
